elements.context: δυνατὴ φύσις ἡ ἀνθρωπίνη ἡ θήλεια

signals.observation: The female/male pair shifts from dogs (θηλείας/ἄρρενες κυνῶν) to women and men (γυναιξίν/ἀνδράσι) and back to the abstract θήλεια/ἄρρενος at 453a, with the dog analogy providing the bridge.

elements.context: τὸν τῶν σκυλάκων τόκον τε καὶ τροφήν
τὴν αὐτὴν τροφήν τε καὶ παιδείαν
τὴν τῶν γυναικῶν καὶ παίδων κτῆσιν καὶ τροφήν

signals.observation: τροφή appears first for puppy-rearing, then as training/education of animals, then for the rearing of women and children — shifting from literal nurture to civic arrangement.

elements.context: τὸ ἐν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς δὴ γελοῖον
γελοῖον ἄλλο τι ἡγεῖται ἢ τὸ κακόν

signals.observation: γελοῖος appears with striking density across 452a–d, culminating in a redefinition: the ridiculous (γελοῖον) is distinguished from the bad (κακόν).

elements.context: γυμνὰς τὰς γυναῖκας ἐν ταῖς παλαίστραις

signals.observation: γυμνάς for women exercising naked is presented as currently laughable; γυμνούς for men exercising naked is cited as formerly laughable among Greeks, creating a parallel between the two.
Stripping (ἀποδύεσθαι) is set against covering up (συγκαλύπτειν) as the better option, in the context of practice revealing what is superior to mere appearance.

elements.context: τὸ ἐν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς δὴ γελοῖον
ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐν τοῖς λόγοις μηνυθέντος ἀρίστου

signals.observation: The ridiculous 'in the eyes' (ἐν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς) is said to flow away under what is revealed as best 'in argument' (ἐν τοῖς λόγοις).

elements.context: τῇ τοῦ ἄρρενος γένους κοινωνῆσαι εἰς ἅπαντα τὰ ἔργα

signals.observation: κοινῇ appears twice for shared activity (of dogs, then as Glaucon's answer), and κοινωνῆσαι returns at 453a for the question of whether female nature can share in all works.

elements.context: τὰς μὲν οἰκουρεῖν ἔνδον ὡς ἀδυνάτους

signals.observation: The alternative for female dogs — staying indoors as housekeepers (οἰκουρεῖν ἔνδον) on grounds of incapacity (ἀδυνάτους) — is presented as the rejected option in the dog analogy.
The sole qualification to shared work is stated as a comparative pair: weaker (ἀσθενεστέραις) for females, stronger (ἰσχυροτέροις) for males.

elements.context: ἐξῆν τοῖς τότε ἀστείοις πάντα ταῦτα κωμῳδεῖν

signals.observation: A cluster of mockery-words: σκώμματα of the witty, κωμῳδεῖν by the urbane of the past, and γελωτοποιεῖν as an activity judged foolish.

elements.context: μὴ ἔρημα τὰ τοῦ ἑτέρου λόγου πολιορκῆται

signals.observation: Socrates proposes arguing against themselves so the opposing argument is not 'besieged undefended' (ἔρημα … πολιορκῆται) — a military metaphor for dialectical procedure.

elements.form: κατὰ φύσιν ἕκαστον ἕνα ἓν τὸ αὑτοῦ πράττειν

signals.observation: The opposing argument cites the earlier principle (each one doing one thing according to nature) and then asserts that men and women have maximally separated natures, generating a contradiction with shared work.

elements.context: δυνατὴ φύσις ἡ ἀνθρωπίνη ἡ θήλεια

signals.observation: φύσις recurs four times in 453a–c, concentrated in the self-opposing argument about whether nature dictates different work.

elements.context: ἐγὼ πάλαι προορῶν ἐφοβούμην τε καὶ ὤκνουν ἅπτεσθαι τοῦ νόμου

signals.observation: Socrates says he long foresaw and feared and hesitated to touch the law concerning women and children — fear and reluctance paired with foresight (προορῶν).

elements.context: τὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν λόγον ὅστις ποτʼ ἐστίν ἑρμηνεῦσαι

signals.observation: Glaucon asks Socrates to 'interpret' (ἑρμηνεῦσαι) their own argument on their behalf, transferring the role of spokesman.

elements.form: πορευτέον πρὸς τὸ τραχὺ τοῦ νόμου

signals.observation: The argument is described as a journey toward 'the rough part of the law' (τὸ τραχύ τοῦ νόμου) — terrain language applied to legislation.
